source_text: Εἰς τὴν γενέθλιον ἡμέραν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἄδηλον μὲν ἔτι οὖσαν τότε, πρὸ δὲ ὀλίγων ἐτῶν γνωρισθεῖσαν παρά τινων τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς Δύσεως ἐλθόντων καὶ ἀναγγειλάντων. αʹ. Ἃ πάλαι πατριάρχαι μὲν ὤδινον, προφῆται δὲ προὔλεγον, δίκαιοι δὲ ἰδεῖν ἐπεθύμουν, ταῦτα ἐξέβη, καὶ τέλος ἔλαβε σήμερον· καὶ Θεὸς ἐπὶ γῆς ὤφθη διὰ σαρκὸς, καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις συνανεστράφη. Χαίρωμεν τοίνυν καὶ ἀγαλλιώμεθα, ἀγαπητοί. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐν τῇ νηδύϊ τῆς μητρὸς ὢν, τῆς Μαρίας εἰσελθούσης πρὸς τὴν Ἐλισάβετ, ἐσκίρτησε· πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἡμᾶς οὐχὶ τὴν Μαρίαν, ἀλλ' αὐτὸν τὸν Σωτῆρα ἡμῶν σήμερον τεχθέντα θεασαμένους, σκιρτᾷν καὶ ἀγάλλεσθαι χρὴ καὶ θαυμάζειν καὶ ἐκπλήττεσθαι τῆς οἰκονομίας τὸ μέγεθος πᾶσαν ὑπερβαῖνον διάνοιαν. Ἐννόησον γὰρ ἡλίκον ἐστὶν, ἥλιον ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν καταβάντα, ἐπὶ γῆς τρέχοντα ὁρᾷν, καὶ τὰς ἀκτῖνας πᾶσιν ἀφιέντα ἐντεῦθεν. Εἰ δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ αἰσθητοῦ φωστῆρος τοῦτο συμβὰν πάντας ἐξέπληξεν ἂν τοὺς θεωμένους, σκόπει μοι καὶ λογίζου νῦν, ἡλίκον ἐστὶ τὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἥλιον ἐκ τῆς ἡμετέρας σαρκὸς ἀφιέντα τὰς ἀκτῖνας ὁρᾷν, καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν καταυγάζοντα. Πάλαι ταύτην ἐπεθύμουν ἐγὼ τὴν ἡμέραν ἰδεῖν, καὶ οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἰδεῖν, ἀλλὰ μετὰ πλήθους τοσούτου· καὶ διηνεκῶς ηὐχόμην οὕτως ἡμῖν πληρωθῆναι τὸ θέατρον, ὥσπερ ἔστι νῦν ὁρᾷν πεπληρωμένον. Τοῦτο τοίνυν ἐξέβη καὶ τέλος ἔλαβε. Καίτοι γε οὔπω δέκατόν ἐστιν ἔτος, ἐξ οὗ δήλη καὶ γνώριμος ἡμῖν αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα γεγένηται· ἀλλ' ὅμως, ὡς ἄνωθεν καὶ πρὸ πολλῶν ἡμῖν παραδοθεῖσα ἐτῶν, οὕτως ἤνθησε διὰ τῆς ὑμετέρας σπουδῆς. Ὅθεν οὐκ ἄν τις ἁμάρτοι καὶ νέαν αὐτὴν ὁμοῦ καὶ ἀρχαίαν προσειπών· νέαν μὲν διὰ τὸ προσφάτως ἡμῖν γνωρισθῆναι, παλαιὰν δὲ καὶ ἀρχαίαν διὰ τὸ ταῖς πρεσβυτέραις ταχέως ὁμήλικα γενέσθαι, καὶ πρὸς τὸ αὐτὸ τῆς ἡλικίας αὐταῖς φθάσαι μέτρον. Καθάπερ γὰρ τὰ γενναῖα καὶ εὐγενῆ τῶν φυτῶν (καὶ γὰρ ἐκεῖνα ὁμοῦ τε εἰς τὴν γῆν κατατίθεται, καὶ πρὸς ὕψος εὐθὺς ἀνατρέχει μέγα, καὶ τῷ καρπῷ βρίθεται), οὕτω καὶ αὕτη παρὰ μὲν τοῖς τὴν Ἑσπέραν οἰκοῦσιν ἄνωθεν γνωριζομένη, πρὸς ἡμᾶς δὲ κομισθεῖσα νῦν, καὶ οὐ πρὸ πολλῶν ἐτῶν, ἀθρόον οὕτως ἀνέδραμε, καὶ τοσοῦτον ἤνεγκε τὸν καρπὸν, ὅσονπερ ἔστι νῦν ὁρᾷν, τῶν περιβόλων ἡμῖν πεπληρωμένων, καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἁπάσης στενοχωρουμένης τῷ πλήθει τῶν συνδραμόντων. Τὴν μὲν οὖν ἀξίαν ἀμοιβὴν τῆς τοσαύτης σπουδῆς παρὰ τοῦ σήμερον τεχθέντος κατὰ σάρκα προσδοκήσατε Χριστοῦ· ἐκεῖνος ὑμᾶς ἀμείψεται πάντως τῆς προθυμίας ταύτης· ἡ γὰρ περὶ τὴν ἡμέραν φιλία καὶ σπουδὴ, τῆς περὶ τὸν τεχθέντα ἀγάπης μέγιστόν ἐστι σημεῖον. Εἰ δὲ χρή τινα καὶ παρ' ἡμῶν τῶν συνδούλων εἰσενεχθῆναι, καὶ ἡμεῖς τὰ κατὰ δύναμιν εἰσοίσομεν· μᾶλλον δὲ, ἅπερ ἂν ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ χάρις δῷ λεχθῆναι διὰ τὴν ὠφέλειαν τὴν ὑμετέραν. Τί οὖν ἐπιθυμεῖτε ἀκοῦσαι σήμερον; τί δὲ ἄλλο, ἢ περὶ τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης; Εὖ γὰρ οἶδα, ὅτι πολλοὶ ἔτι καὶ νῦν πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἀμφισβητοῦσιν, οἱ μὲν ἐγκαλοῦντες, οἱ δὲ ἀπολογούμενοι· καὶ πολὺς περὶ τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης πανταχοῦ γίνεται λόγος, τῶν μὲν αἰτιωμένων, ὅτι νέα τίς ἐστι καὶ πρόσφατος, καὶ νῦν εἰσενήνεκται, τῶν δὲ ἀπολογουμένων, ὅτι παλαιὰ καὶ ἀρχαία ἐστὶ, τῶν προφητῶν ἤδη προειπόντων περὶ τῆς γεννήσεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἄνωθεν τοῖς ἀπὸ Θρᾴκης μέχρι Γαδείρων οἰκοῦσι κατάδηλος καὶ ἐπίσημος γέγονε.
thought_title: The feast newly known yet ancient
orientation: John Chrysostom opens his homily for the feast of Christ's Nativity, addressing the congregation gathered in the church.
pass_a_gloss: For the Christmas Day of our Savior Jesus Christ, being still unclear then, but made known a few years before by some of those who came from the West and announced it. Section 1. What patriarchs of old were in labor with, and prophets foretold, and righteous men desired to see, these things came to pass, and received their fulfillment today; and God was seen on earth through flesh, and lived among human beings. Let us rejoice therefore and be glad, beloved. For if John, being in the womb of his mother, when Mary entered to Elizabeth, leaped; much more must we, having beheld not Mary, but our Savior himself born today, leap and be glad and marvel and be astonished at the greatness of the plan of salvation surpassing every thought. For consider how great a thing it is, to see the sun having come down from the heavens, running upon the earth, and sending forth its rays to all from there. But if this having happened in the case of the perceptible luminary would have astonished all who beheld it, consider for me and reckon now, how great a thing it is to see the Sun of Righteousness sending forth rays from our flesh, and illuminating our souls. Long ago I was desiring to see this day, and not simply to see it, but with so great a multitude; and continually I was praying that the theater be filled for us in this way, just as it is now possible to see it filled. This therefore came to pass and received its fulfillment. And yet it is not yet the tenth year, from which this day has become clear and known to us; but nevertheless, as if handed down to us from above and before many years, so it has blossomed through your zeal. Whence one would not err in calling it at once new and ancient; new because of its having been made known to us recently, but old and ancient because of its having quickly become coeval with the older feasts, and having reached the same measure of age as them. For just as the noble and well-born of plants (for those too are at once placed into the earth, and immediately run up to a great height, and are weighed down with fruit), so also this feast, being known from above among those who inhabit the West, but brought to us now, and not many years ago, has suddenly so run up, and has borne so much fruit, as much as it is now possible to see, our precincts being filled, and the whole church being crowded by the multitude of those who have run together. Expect therefore the worthy recompense of so great zeal from Christ born today according to the flesh; he will repay you altogether for this eagerness; for the affection and zeal concerning the day is the greatest sign of love for the one born. But if something must also be contributed by us your fellow-servants, we too will contribute what is in our power; or rather, whatever the grace of God may grant to be said for your benefit. What then do you desire to hear today? What else, than about this day? For I know well that many even now dispute with one another, some accusing, some defending; and much talk about this day happens everywhere, some alleging that it is new and recent, and has now been introduced, others defending that it is old and ancient, the prophets having already foretold about his birth, and from above it has become clear and notable to those who dwell from Thrace as far as Gades.

pass_b_english: On the Christmas Day of our Savior Jesus Christ—a day still unknown at that time, but made known a few years earlier by some who came from the West and announced it. What patriarchs long ago labored to bring forth, what prophets foretold, what righteous people longed to see—these things have come to pass and reached their fulfillment today. God has appeared on earth in the flesh and lived among human beings (Baruch 3:38). So let us rejoice and be glad, beloved. If John, while still in his mother's womb, leaped when Mary entered Elizabeth's house (Luke 1:41), how much more should we—who have seen not Mary but our Savior Himself born today—leap and rejoice and marvel and be astonished at the greatness of the plan of salvation, which surpasses every thought. Consider how great a thing it is to see the sun come down from the heavens and run upon the earth, sending out its rays to all from here. If this happened with the visible light and it would have astounded everyone who saw it, then consider and reckon now how great a thing it is to see the Sun of Righteousness sending out His rays from our own flesh and illuminating our souls (Malachi 4:2). I have long desired to see this day—and not simply to see it, but to see it with so great a crowd. I prayed constantly that our theater would be filled for us just as you can see it filled now. This has come to pass and reached its fulfillment. And yet it is not yet ten years since this day became clear and known to us. But all the same, as if it had been handed down to us from the beginning and many years ago, so it has blossomed through your zeal. So no one would be wrong to call it both new and ancient at once: new because it has only recently been made known to us, but old and ancient because it quickly became coeval with the older feasts and reached the same measure of age as they have. Just as noble and well-bred plants—for they are placed in the ground and at once shoot up to a great height and are weighed down with fruit—so this feast, known from the beginning among those who dwell in the West but brought to us only now and not many years ago, has suddenly run up so high and borne so much fruit as you can see now: our precincts are filled, and the whole church is crowded with the multitude of those who have gathered. Expect, then, a worthy reward for such zeal from Christ, who was born today in the flesh. He will certainly repay you for this eagerness, for love and zeal for the day is the greatest sign of love for the One who was born. And if something should also be offered by us, your fellow-servants, we too will offer what we can—or rather, whatever God's grace grants to be said for your benefit. What then do you desire to hear today? What else but about this day? For I know well that many even now dispute with one another, some accusing and some defending, and there is much talk everywhere about this day: some charge that it is new and recent and has only now been introduced, while others defend it as old and ancient, since the prophets already foretold His birth, and from the beginning it has been clear and well known to those who dwell from Thrace to Gades.

last_rejected.why: Baruch 3:38 does not match the Greek wording; this is a loose allusion, not a direct citation of Baruch.
last_rejected.fix: Remove the scripture reference or verify against LXX Baruch 3:37-38.
last_rejected.ruling: Baruch 3:38 LXX closely matches: ἐπὶ γῆς ὤφθη καὶ ἀνθρώποις συνανεστράφη—valid citation.

last_rejected.quote: leaped when Mary entered Elizabeth's house (Luke 1:41)
last_rejected.source_quote: τῆς Μαρίας εἰσελθούσης πρὸς τὴν Ἐλισάβετ, ἐσκίρτησε
last_rejected.why: Source says Mary entered to Elizabeth, not Elizabeth's house; 'house' is added.
last_rejected.fix: leaped when Mary entered to see Elizabeth (Luke 1:41)
last_rejected.ruling: 'πρὸς τὴν Ἐλισάβετ' idiomatically means entering Elizabeth's home; 'house' is normal rendering.

last_rejected.why: 'τρέχοντα' here means 'moving, traversing,' not 'run'; sun does not run on earth.
last_rejected.ruling: τρέχοντα literally means 'running'; metaphorical use for sun's course is standard, not an error.

last_rejected.why: 'φωστῆρος' means 'luminary, light-giver,' not abstract 'light'; refers to the sun as visible body.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Visible light' adequately renders αἰσθητοῦ φωστῆρος; 'luminary' is preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: 'βρίθεται' means 'burdened, laden,' but in context of noble plants it suggests abundance, not being weighed down as problem.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Weighed down with fruit' is standard rendering of τῷ καρπῷ βρίθεται; abundance is implied, not lost.
